A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TTRL, and their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison. Retained content can be matched despite substantial reorganization and expanded experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original TTRL evaluations on AIME 2024, AMC and MATH-500, together with transfer experiments, training dynamics and ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations including GPQA-Diamond, additional backbone and reasoning models, and training-dynamics analyses, alongside retained earlier results.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2, Equations 1–3 and Listing 1 retain the same sampling, majority-vote label estimation, binary reward and policy-update framework. PRIME expands the algorithm-compatibility evaluation; no new component of the proposed consensus-reward procedure is specified.

E1.justification: v3 adds GPQA-Diamond, extending evaluation from mathematical reasoning to graduate-level question answering. AIME 2024, AMC, MATH-500 and the original cross-benchmark transfer scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 add direct comparisons against unadapted Qwen2.5-7B/32B, Qwen3-8B and additional LLaMA, Mistral, DeepSeek and Skywork models. Figure 5 adds PRIME to the corresponding GRPO/PPO comparison. The earlier R1-like reference-model comparisons largely survive in Appendix A.

E3.justification: Main evaluation changes from greedy decoding to sampled pass@1 using 16 responses, or four for 32k context, with temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95; greedy supplementary evaluations remain. Reported training changes include constant-to-cosine learning rate, 16-to-32 training responses per prompt, and MATH/AMC/AIME episodes changing from 40/50/60 to 10/30/80. Additional model configurations and 32k reasoning-model contexts substantially expand the settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds AMC avg@16/maj@16 training trajectories to examine whether individual-answer improvements compromise majority-vote performance, and extends algorithm compatibility to PRIME. Existing transfer, difficulty-level, labeled-RL upper-bound, reward-accuracy and hyperparameter analyses remain, so these are targeted extensions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent training-run replication, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical error bars. Sampled-response averaging already appears in v1; v3's changed main evaluation sample counts belong to the evaluation protocol rather than a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results include Qwen3-8B thinking-mode AIME accuracy of 72.5 to 82.5 and Qwen2.5-Math-7B GPQA accuracy of 29.1 to 27.7. Original greedy Qwen results remain unchanged in v3 Table 4, while the greedy LLaMA rows are omitted; new main-table scores use different conditions. The successful-attempt and temperature-0.6 trajectories also exchange assignments between v1 Figure 10 and v3 Figure 11.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the appendix definitions of test-time training and inference are retained. No theorem, proof or formal assumption is added. The new pass@1 formula explains a standard metric, while the online-learning discussion remains conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract's headline AIME improvement changes from approximately 159% to 211%, and the introduction changes from an 84% average gain over three mathematical benchmarks to 76% over four benchmarks including GPQA. These claims use revised evaluation conditions. The central contributions of unlabeled RL, exceeding initial majority-vote performance and approaching labeled-test-data RL remain.

C2.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 add an explicit online-feedback explanation in which improving models generate better supervision, and distinguish TTRL from a claimed traditional self-training ceiling. 'Lucky Hit' largely elaborates the existing negative-reward explanation. The earlier attribution of specific small-model AIME failures to insufficient priors is removed, while general prior-knowledge and hyperparameter limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix B's detailed OpenRLHF recipe is removed, losing batch and microbatch sizes, critic learning rate, gamma/lambda, KL coefficient, prompt-length limit and optimization flags. v3 adds hardware information specifying eight A100 80GB GPUs and revised settings in Section 3.1, but provides no equivalent replacement recipe. The code link is unchanged; omitted settings do not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: Section 5.2 substantially expands positioning against self-rewarding, self-play, preference optimization and concurrent unsupervised reasoning work, including GENIUS and Absolute Zero, plus single-example RL. Section 4.1 adds a comparison with Huang et al.'s self-training approach. These additions materially clarify the claimed distinctions from closely related research.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten, and the experimental narrative and mechanism discussion are reorganized. Training metrics move from Section 3.3 to Appendix B, earlier benchmark comparisons move to Appendix A, and terminology moves to Appendix C. The failure-condition arguments are reordered and the reward explanation is extensively revised.

P2.justification: The main table is redesigned with GPQA and model-group headings, and a model-comparison table plus reasoning-model and training-dynamics figures are added. Earlier results and curves move to Appendix A, the configuration table disappears, and several retained plots receive revised axes, legends, numerical labels or captions.

improvement.justification: The broader task and reasoning-model evaluations strengthen support for TTRL's generality, while clearer evaluation procedures and fuller related-work comparisons improve assessment of its contribution. These gains are tempered by removal of the detailed training recipe and new numerical overstatements: Section 4.1 claims a margin above 20 points where Figure 6 shows only a few, and Section 3.2's minimum 105% improvement conflicts with Qwen3's 73.6% in Table 1. The net improvement is therefore limited.
